preconditions: The victim loads a FlatBuffers binary reflection schema (.bfbs) with the flatbuffers reflection API — either the flatc compiler (supply-chain / build-time), or any application using flatbuffers::Parser::Deserialize / reflection at runtime (e.g. a service that accepts schemas from clients).

The .bfbs carries a Field whose reflection `id` (reflection.fbs: `id:ushort;`) is greater than or equal to its parent Object's field count. `id` is a plain uint16 with no cross-check against the field vector length, so a structurally-valid buffer passes the flatbuffers Verifier unchanged.
The library is built with any standard optimizing configuration (the shipped default); the bug is the unguarded `indexes[of.Get(i)->id()] = i` write.

evidence.vulnerable_version: every release through v25.12.19-2026-02-06 (95fda8c, 2026-02-06) and v25.12.19 (282dcb1) — the latest tagged releases
evidence.fixed_version: unreleased (master only; the bounds check 8a12183 merged 2026-04-02 is not an ancestor of any release tag)
evidence.observed_result: poc.cc drives the vendored v25.12.19-2026-02-06 reflection parser (real src/idl_parser.cpp + reflection.cpp + util.cpp) through Parser::Deserialize on a structurally-valid .bfbs whose single field has id=1 (field count=1). The vulnerable loop writes indexes[1] one uoffset_t past the 4-byte heap vector, corrupting the redzone canary placed by poc.cc's instrumented allocator (0xcd -> 0x00 at byte +4). With id=0xFFFF the same write lands ~256 KiB past the buffer and the process dies with SIGSEGV. The fixed build (upstream 8a12183 applied) rejects the identical buffer with 'Field ID 1 exceeds field count 1' and performs no out-of-bounds write.

real_exploit.backend: real project source vendored verbatim from tag v25.12.19-2026-02-06 (95fda8c): src/idl_parser.cpp, src/reflection.cpp, src/util.cpp, and include/flatbuffers/*.h, compiled with zig cc. poc.cc crafts a structurally-valid .bfbs using the library's own reflection::CreateSchema/CreateField builders (id = attacker value) and feeds it to flatbuffers::Parser::Deserialize; a redzone-canary global operator new/delete turns the out-of-bounds write into a deterministic observable.
real_exploit.demonstrated: The real reflection parser writes one uoffset_t past the `indexes` heap vector (redzone canary 0xcd->0x00 detected), and with a large attacker id (0xFFFF) the write is ~256 KiB out of bounds and terminates the process with SIGSEGV. The upstream-fixed code rejects the same .bfbs with a bounds error and leaves memory untouched. This is a heap out-of-bounds WRITE (CWE-787) with an attacker-controlled offset (field id * 4, up to ~256 KiB) and a small attacker-influenceable value (the field loop index).

notes: 0-day: the fix 8a12183 (2026-04-02) is not an ancestor of the latest release tag v25.12.19-2026-02-06. Impact is a heap OOB write; full RCE is not demonstrated (needs heap grooming to pivot the limited-value write into control-flow hijack), but the demonstrated effect is deterministic memory corruption + crash in the reflection parser.
